cards.title: Menthol doesn't physically lower temperature—it tricks your cold sensors
cards.body: When you chew mint gum or apply menthol balm, your mouth or skin feels icy cold, but its actual temperature does not drop. Menthol molecules bind directly to TRPM8, a specialized ion channel protein on sensory neurons that normally detects temperatures below 26°C (79°F). By chemically unlocking this receptor, menthol sends false electrical signals to your brain, creating an illusion of intense cold without removing any thermal energy.

sources.title: TRPM8: The Cold and Menthol Receptor

cards.title: Why your joints feel stiff after sitting still and loosen as you walk
cards.body: The fluid lubricating your knees and hips, called synovial fluid, is non-Newtonian and thixotropic—its viscosity changes under mechanical stress. When you sit stationary for hours, synovial fluid thickens into a gel-like consistency, making your joints feel stiff upon standing. As you start moving, the shearing forces generated by joint articulation thin the fluid out into a slippery lubricant, dramatically reducing friction within just a few minutes of walking.

cards.title: A single structural protein makes up 30 percent of your body's total protein
cards.body: Collagen is the primary structural scaffold of the human body, accounting for roughly 30% of your total protein mass and nearly three-quarters of your dry skin weight. Organized into rigid triple-helix molecular ropes, collagen fibers provide tensile strength to skin, bones, tendons, ligaments, and blood vessels. Because the body's natural collagen synthesis declines steadily after early adulthood, tissues gradually lose elasticity, contributing to skin wrinkles and stiffer joints.

cards.title: The tiny valve in your throat that stops your eardrums from bursting
cards.body: Your middle ear is an air-filled chamber sealed off from the outside world by the eardrum. To keep pressure balanced on both sides, the Eustachian tube connects the middle ear directly to the back of your throat (nasopharynx). This channel normally stays pinched shut to block pathogens, but swallowing, chewing, or yawning activates small palate muscles that pull the valve open, releasing trapped air and equalizing pressure so atmospheric changes do not rupture delicate hearing membranes.

sources.title: Anatomy, Head and Neck, Eustachian Tube

cards.title: Why eating extra protein doesn't mean your body stores extra muscle
cards.body: Unlike carbohydrates stored as glycogen or dietary fats stored in adipose tissue, the human body possesses no specialized storage reservoir for excess protein. Once immediate structural needs and protein synthesis targets are met, the liver strips nitrogen from surplus amino acids through a process called deamination. The resulting nitrogen is converted into urea and excreted in urine, while the remaining carbon skeletons are burned for immediate energy or converted into glucose and fat.

quizzes.question: How does menthol make your mouth feel cold without physically lowering its temperature?
options: It binds directly to the TRPM8 cold-sensing receptor on nerve cells
It triggers rapid evaporation of saliva from the tongue
It constricts blood vessels to reduce oral blood flow
It temporarily blocks heat-sensing pain receptors
quizzes.explanation: Menthol chemically unlocks the TRPM8 ion channel, sending cold signals to the brain even though the actual temperature hasn't changed.

quizzes.question: Why does synovial fluid inside your joints thin out and lubricate better after you start walking?
options: It is thixotropic and becomes less viscous when subjected to mechanical shear stress
Body heat boils off excess water in the joint capsule
The joint absorbs calcium crystals that previously caused friction
Muscles pump extra lymphatic fluid into the joint cavity
quizzes.explanation: Synovial fluid is non-Newtonian and thixotropic: resting makes it thick and gel-like, while movement thins it out to lubricate joints.

quizzes.question: Roughly what proportion of the human body's total protein mass consists of collagen?
options: About 30%
About 5%
About 60%
About 85%
quizzes.explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the body, making up about 30% of total protein mass and 75% of dry skin weight.

quizzes.question: Which structure equalizes air pressure between your middle ear and the atmosphere when you swallow or yawn?
options: The Eustachian tube
The cochlear duct
The carotid canal
The tympanic sinus
quizzes.explanation: The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the back of the throat and opens during swallowing to balance middle ear pressure.

quizzes.question: What does the liver do with dietary amino acids when the body already has enough protein for tissue repair?
options: It removes their nitrogen via deamination and converts the remainder to fuel or fat
It stores them in specialized protein-storing fat cells for up to six months
It sends them directly to the kidneys to be excreted unchanged in urine
It binds them together into inert storage filaments inside bone marrow
quizzes.explanation: The body cannot store protein; excess amino acids undergo deamination in the liver, turning into urea and energy substrates.

guesses.prompt: What percentage of the human body's total protein mass is made up of collagen?
guesses.explanation: Collagen makes up about 30% of all protein in the human body, providing the structural scaffold for skin, bones, and tendons.

misconceptions.claim: Menthol mints cool your mouth by causing a physical drop in surface temperature.
misconceptions.explanation: Menthol does not remove heat; it chemically stimulates the TRPM8 sensory channel, tricking your brain into feeling cold.

misconceptions.claim: The human body stores excess dietary protein in dedicated reserves for future muscle growth.
misconceptions.explanation: The body has no protein storage reservoir; surplus amino acids are deaminated and burned as fuel or converted into fat.
